macro.narrative: Re-anchored 7 Aug from an in-session run. Covers through the 6 Aug US close. The 7 Aug Asia session is NOT included — this run gathered data on 6 Aug and the 7 Aug sessions had not closed when it was verified. The 4 Aug de-escalation trade has NOT settled: the S&P made its record 7,736.52 on 4 Aug, edged off it on 5 Aug, then fell on 6 Aug as Brent rebounded ~4% on renewed Hormuz concern — even though WTI is still down ~11% over three sessions to ~$75 after Iran and Oman agreed a shipping route. The bigger shift is the Fed: September is now priced roughly 65% for a HIKE, not a cut, after a 9-3 July vote and Governor Cook saying plainly that inflation is too high and she is prepared to raise. ISM Services printed 54.1 with Prices at 70.3 and Employment back in contraction at 47.4 — stagflation-lite — while Challenger layoffs hit a two-year low and claims held under 200k, denying the Fed any labour-market cover to ease. Yet precious metals rallied straight through the hawkish repricing: silver $62.20 and gold $4,270.62 (+2.38%), the first open above $4,300 since 17 July. Asia diverged violently: Korea crashed -4.58% (SK Hynix -10.37%), the Hang Seng fell 1.5%, but Shanghai bucked it and DBS posted a record S$3.08b quarter and RAISED FY guidance.

drivers.factor: September FOMC priced for a HIKE (~65%)
drivers.read: Fed Governor Cook 5 Aug: inflation "too high", "prepared to act by raising rates"; July vote was 9-3 with three hike dissents. This is the dominant swing factor and it is hostile to every rate-sensitive sleeve.

drivers.factor: Precious metals rallying INTO the hawkish repricing
drivers.read: Silver $62.20 (from ~$58.5 on 4 Aug) and gold $4,270.62 +2.38%, gold rising even as the 10Y backed up 5bp to 4.67%. The metals are no longer trading purely off real rates — a genuine change of character in the book's largest risk.

WTI -11% over three sessions to ~$75 on an Iran-Oman shipping agreement, but Brent rebounded ~4% on 6 Aug on renewed concern. Oil has round-tripped a meaningful part of the crash; do not treat the risk premium as removed.

drivers.factor: US labour: soft surveys, firm hard data
drivers.read: ADP +44k (weakest of the year) against Challenger layoffs at a two-year low and claims at 199k. Continuing claims rising to 1.801m says the re-hire rate is slowing, but nothing here forces the Fed to ease.
Korea -4.58% with SK Hynix -10.37%, Hang Seng -1.5%, yet Shanghai rose and Japan had run +3.66% on 5 Aug. Single "Asia" exposure is misleading right now; the sleeves must be read separately.

drivers.factor: DBS record quarter and raised guidance
drivers.read: Q2 net profit +9% to a record S$3.08b, quarterly income above S$6b for the first time, FY2026 guidance RAISED. Direct support for the largest single SGX holding.
